clips.text_zh: /biz/又有巴菲特式Saylor詩😂 MSTR同SpaceX一齊舞,BTC繼續亮。10月又係學費月份,睇下我哋prop firm今個月會輸幾多🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Saylor Moon :. In the night, Saylor Moon makes Bitcoin shine, MSTR dances with SpaceX on a divine path. Between the stars and the sats, the portfolio ignites, and toward El Dorado, Saylor Moon unfolds his soul. The thread is a /biz/ poem about BTC and MSTR as a religious path. This came up on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: Saylor Moon rises as /biz/ coins yet another Buffett-style verse, casting Bitcoin as some divine pilgrimage. The poem places MSTR twirling alongside SpaceX while BTC keeps shining, framing the whole portfolio as a quasi-religious calling. It is essentially 4chan treating MSTR and Bitcoin as though they were objects of worship, the same ritual believers repeat whenever markets wobble. This came up on /biz/ today, drawing the usual chorus of worshipful replies.
clips.text_en_c1: A self-styled /biz/ poem has cast Saylor as a quasi-religious figure whose moonward ascent transfigures Bitcoin into something approaching scripture. The verses portray MSTR moving in tandem with SpaceX along an almost providential trajectory, while the portfolio itself becomes a votive offering to El Dorado. Beneath the satirical veneer lies an authentic conviction among certain anons that BTC and MSTR constitute a salvific path worth enshrining. Such deification, the thread implicitly argues, has itself become the dominant folk religion of the board. The post surfaced on /biz/ today, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/biz/thread/62751731
clips.text_en_c2: What began as a throwaway jest on /biz/ has, predictably, metastasised into something approaching liturgical verse. The poem in question casts Michael Saylor as a sort of crypto-Buddha, with MicroStrategy's MSTR gyrating in lockstep with SpaceX as though the two were locked in some holy pas de deux. Bitcoin, naturally, functions as the sacred flame — that ineffable lumen around which the congregation gathers, sats clutched like prayer beads. The conceit is half-ironic, half-genuine, which is to say it is precisely the register that /biz/ has perfected over the years. October being tuition season, anons are already bracing themselves for the customary haemorrhaging of demo accounts at proprietary firms. Whether Saylor is prophet or pied piper remains, as ever, a matter of temperament.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP writes a religious-style poem about Saylor and Bitcoin

clips.text_zh: 100M美金option輸晒,CEO同老婆一齊冇咗。認真,呢個世界揸option真係會死。睇完好驚,prop firm算乜嘢😭
clips.text_en_b1: A fashion executive killed his wife and himself after gambling away $100 million on options. His brother said Paul went behind the family’s back, took loans against their properties, traded risky options, and fell into immense debt. The brother said he had not worked for some time, but they agreed he could play with their wealth. Then he lost control. This was on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: A fashion executive, having gambled away roughly one hundred million dollars on options, ultimately took his own life along with his wife's, a tragedy that shook /biz/ today. His brother revealed that Paul had secretly taken out loans against family properties and spiralled into unmanageable debt, even though they had previously agreed he could speculate with their shared wealth. The thread serves as a grim reminder of how options trading can devastate entire families.
clips.text_en_c1: The fashion executive at the centre of the tragedy allegedly borrowed against jointly owned property without his family's knowledge, plunging the entirety of their holdings into leveraged options positions that subsequently evaporated. By the time the losses had compounded into something approaching a hundred million dollars, reconciliation had become untenable; what followed was an irreversible act whose victims included his wife. His brother, quoted in the thread, described the sequence as a gradual erosion rather than a single ruinous trade. The /biz/ discussion treats the episode as a cautionary parable, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/biz/thread/62751406
clips.text_en_c2: A cautionary tale of the most appalling kind has surfaced on /biz/, the particulars of which ought to give any retail speculator considerable pause. A fashion-industry executive, Paul by name, having apparently wearied of conventional gainful employment, proceeded behind his family's back to encumber their jointly held properties with substantial loans, the proceeds of which were duly funnelled into a highly leveraged options book. The outcome was, in retrospect, inevitable: roughly one hundred million dollars evaporated, leaving in their wake a debris field of personal ruin so total that the man subsequently took both his wife's life and his own. His brother, recounting the episode with admirable restraint, noted that the family had consented to let him "play" with their capital — a euphemism whose tragic inadequacy speaks for itself.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ shares NY Post story on fashion CEO who lost $100M on options

clips.text_zh: /pol/又串中國lol 'first-world country until fix weird shit'。我都覺香港同大陸一樣,地方細到痴線,等5年後返美國🙏
clips.text_en_b1: China will never be a first-world country until it fixes its weird yet funny shit. The /pol/ thread collects the latest clips and stories about strange behaviour in mainland China. It is the same argument 4chan has been making for years about living standards. The thread went up on /pol/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: /pol/ has dusted off its familiar refrain: China will never qualify as a first-world country until it sorts out its bizarre yet darkly comedic behaviour. The thread compiles clips and anecdotes illustrating how mainland daily life still falls short of Western living standards, recycling the same argument 4chan has been peddling for years. While the tone is mocking, plenty of anons pile in to share their own equally strange encounters, keeping the debate very much alive today.
clips.text_en_c1: The /pol/ thread revisits a familiar refrain: that China will remain permanently consigned to second-tier status until the more bewildering aspects of daily life are brought to heel. Anons compile clips and anecdotes illustrating behaviour that, while ostensibly humorous, underscores genuine concerns about urban density, regulatory overreach, and civic disorder. The argument is hardly novel—4chan has rehearsed it ad nauseam—yet it retains a stubborn appeal, particularly among expatriates weighing whether to remain abroad. The post emerged on /pol/ today, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/pol/thread/543784160
clips.text_en_c2: A familiar refrain has once more wafted up from the fetid depths of /pol/: China, it seems, shall remain permanently consigned to the second tier of nations until such time as it deigns to rectify its manifold eccentricities. The thread, which surfaces periodically with the regularity of a recurring fever, assembles the latest footage and anecdotes documenting behaviour that ranges from the merely baffling to the outright dystopian. The underlying thesis — that material modernisation is not, in itself, synonymous with civilisational maturity — is hardly novel; indeed, it is the same argument these quarters have been propounding for the better part of two decades, with diminishing returns. For any expatriate presently marooned in the mainland or its special-administrative adjunct, the prognosis remains grim.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread collecting weird funny Chinese clips

clips.text_zh: /g/話2026年仲冇打掃機械人,得Optimus可以救大家。AI殺白領先,blue collar都唔會safe,我哋engineer小心啲🧐
clips.text_en_b1: How come there is no technology for doing house chores like cleaning in 2026? Are we stuck with those Optimus robots as our only potential hope towards an actual useful physical assistant? The /g/ thread is asking why domestic robots still do not exist outside of demos. This came up on /g/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: Why, in 2026, do we still lack functional robots capable of handling mundane chores like vacuuming or laundry? The /g/ thread laments that, outside of polished Optimus demos, genuinely useful domestic assistants remain stuck in the realm of vapourware. While AI is busy hollowing out white-collar work, the prospect of blue-collar automation feels equally unsettling, leaving engineers wondering whether their own roles might eventually fall to algorithms. The discussion resurfaced on /g/ today, drawing the usual scepticism.
clips.text_en_c1: Anons on /g/ have once again broached a question that grows only more conspicuous with each passing year: why, in 2026, does no commercially viable domestic cleaning robot exist? The consensus appears resigned to the proposition that Tesla's Optimus represents the most credible option on the table, even as proprietary alternatives should accelerate toward an actual real product. Beneath the irony lies genuine anxiety that AI will first displace white-collar knowledge work and subsequently encroach upon blue-collar trades, and that even engineers themselves should beware. The thread surfaced on /g/ today, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/g/thread/109984759
clips.text_en_c2: The denizens of /g/, never particularly celebrated for their patience, have lately voiced a grievance both mundane and, upon reflection, entirely legitimate: why, in the year of our lord 2026, does no commercially viable domestic robot exist to perform the dreary minutiae of household upkeep? The thread's OP, exhibiting that peculiar blend of despair and faint optimism endemic to the board, has nominated Tesla's Optimus as the only conceivable candidate, a judgement that says as much about the barrenness of the field as it does about the platform's promise. While artificial intelligence continues its inexorable march through the white-collar professions, those labouring in trades once considered impervious to automation would do well to harbour no illusions. Engineers, needless to say, are scarcely insulated from the oncoming gale.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on missing house chore robots and Optimus as last hope

clips.text_zh: /fit/有兄弟starvemaxx到60kg,love handle都減唔到。睇完好驚,我都係繼續跟肥仔信gym plan,慢慢嚟lol
clips.text_en_b1: What if you just starvemaxx till you reach 60kg with like 1 meal per day. Obviously, you'll lose muscle but then in theory you could start rebuilding it rather easy because of muscle memory. He is at his wit's end, skinny fat dyel who tried bulking, cutting, all of them just make him look fat and retarded. This came up on /fit/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: A desperate /fit/ anon starvemaxxed down to sixty kilograms, surviving on roughly one meal a day, yet stubborn love handles still clung on. Although the extreme cut inevitably cost him considerable muscle, he reasoned that muscle memory should eventually allow him to rebuild what was lost. He describes himself as a skinny-fat dyel who has tried everything from aggressive bulking to strict cutting, and nothing seems to work. The thread surfaced on /fit/ today.
clips.text_en_c1: One anonymous /fit/ poster, having descended to roughly sixty kilograms through sustained caloric deprivation, now confronts the paradox of remaining skinny-fat despite achieving an ostensibly lean frame. His regimen—bulking cycles, aggressive cuts, and a single daily meal—has paradoxically produced the very aesthetic he sought to escape, while his love handles have stubbornly persisted regardless of the energy deficit. The thread constitutes an unintentional cautionary tale against what the board calls starvemaxxing, and it has given pause to readers who might otherwise pursue similar shortcuts. The post went up on /fit/ today, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/fit/thread/77542132
clips.text_en_c2: A thread on /fit/ has occasioned not inconsiderable alarm among the more impressionable denizens of the board, its protagonist having undertaken a regimen of severe caloric deprivation so as to reach a skeletal sixty kilograms — only to discover, with mounting horror, that his love handles persist in their tenancy of his flanks. The poster, a self-described skinny-fat novice who has dutifully cycled through bulk and cut phases to no discernible end, now finds himself adrift in that particular purgatory familiar to dilettantes everywhere. The prevailing wisdom, as ever, counsels a return to the fundamentals espoused by seasoned gym-going pudgies: progressive overload, adequate protein, and the cultivation of patience — virtues which, however unglamorous, remain the sine qua non of any meaningful corporeal transformation.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ anon asking about extreme starvation cut to lose love handles

clips.text_en_b1: Ranma 1/2 storytime. Going to storytime the manga in conjunction with the new anime season so anons can compare and contrast, or experience the story in multiple different ways simultaneously. Today the OP is covering chapter 51-52. This came up on /a/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: A dedicated /a/ anon is storytiming the Ranma 1/2 manga alongside the freshly aired anime season, enabling readers to compare and contrast both versions in real time. Today's instalment covers chapters fifty-one and fifty-two, with the OP encouraging others to experience the story through multiple formats simultaneously. Even viewers who never followed Ranma are tuning in, particularly since Attack on Titan appears to be approaching its finale, and they are hoping to catch both tonight.
clips.text_en_c1: A diligent /a/ OP has undertaken to storytime the Ranma 1/2 manga in lockstep with the broadcast of its newly adapted season, thereby affording anons the rare opportunity to compare and contrast the source material against its animated counterpart as they are released. Today's instalment covers chapters fifty-one and fifty-two, in which the curse's further complications are elaborated. While not every participant is instinctively familiar with Ranma, the broader discourse encompasses the imminent conclusion of Attack on Titan, which has generated its own anticipation. The thread surfaced on /a/ today, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/a/thread/291385397
clips.text_en_c2: A /a/ poster has embarked upon the sort of multimedia exegesis that the board rarely sees executed with any discernible discipline: a parallel reading of Takahashi's Ranma ½ manga, conducted in lockstep with the newly launched anime season, so that anons might luxuriate in the story across multiple formats concurrently. Today the enterprising OP is dissecting chapters fifty-one and fifty-two, inviting comparison between Takahashi's original panel work and the studio's contemporary adaptation. Whether one is inclined to follow the resurrected classic or, alternatively, to await the purported finale of Attack on Titan — another matter altogether — depends entirely on one's appetite for closure. For the uncommitted viewer, the evening's viewing list grows ever more crowded.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread storytiming Ranma 1/2 chapters alongside new anime

clips.text_zh: /biz/話Bitcoin永遠唔會大升因為有'showman'做代表。即係話Elon一日做Bitcoin代表,BTC就一世都唔會爆升lol 真係笑死人
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin will never pump to unreal amounts as long as this showman is the face of it. The /biz/ OP is saying that as long as Elon Musk is still the public face of Bitcoin, BTC cannot do a true blowoff top. The thread is mostly anons agreeing and dunking on Musk. This came up on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: According to a /biz/ thread, Bitcoin will never achieve a genuine blowoff top as long as this particular showman remains its public face. The argument goes that, while Elon Musk continues to represent the cryptocurrency in mainstream media, BTC simply cannot pump to the stratospheric levels enthusiasts dream about. Most anons piled in to agree, cheerfully dunking on Musk's every tweet, because the thread quickly devolved into a roast session. This came up on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_c1: The OP on /biz/ advances a thesis that has gained considerable traction: that Bitcoin will never achieve its long-anticipated blowoff top so long as Elon Musk remains its most conspicuous public advocate. The argument holds that the executive's conspicuous demeanour has rendered BTC a parody of itself, and that only his permanent removal would allow genuine price discovery to materialise. Most respondents concur, and the thread has consequently devolved into ritualised mockery of Musk rather than substantive market analysis. The post went up on /biz/ today, the source_url: https://boards.4chan.org/biz/thread/62752885
clips.text_en_c2: A /biz/ thread has lately advanced the heretical proposition that Bitcoin, that great engine of speculative fervour, shall never achieve its longed-for blowoff top so long as a certain showman remains affixed to its public image. The argument, such as it is, posits that Elon Musk's garrulous evangelism functions less as a catalyst for genuine institutional adoption than as a kind of tawdry carnival barker — sufficient perhaps to part the credulous from their sats, but wholly inadequate to the task of seducing serious capital. The thread's participants, predictably, have responded with the customary fusillade of mockery, dunking upon the man with the alacrity one might expect from a constituency long practised in the art. Whether the diagnosis is correct is, charitably, an open question.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread saying BTC cannot pump while Musk is its face
